applicabilityBasis.summary: BUCK is the legacy dollar-linked Bucket CDP debt unit, with protocol migration into successor USDB at 1:1. Stablecoin use is not limited to an accounting receipt, but the reviewed migration and interface terms do not establish an identified legal issuer obligated to convert, redeem or repurchase BUCK for a fixed amount of monetary value under GENIUS section 2(22). Token-to-token migration does not supply that obligation; applicability remains unclear rather than treating all CDPs as exempt.

genius.notes: Scope concerns legacy Sui BUCK, not Bucket successor USDB or the unrelated buck.io/Buck Token. Exact legal token issuer and domicile remain unresolved; issuerEntity is intentionally omitted rather than setting it to Bucket Protocol Team or inferring Seychelles incorporation from contract law. Terms exclude US interface users but do not establish a statutory exemption or prevent independent token transfers. Migration phases are documented, not dated proof that exit-only mode has begun. No public fiat-par redemption undertaking or monthly financial-statement attestation was located; optional disclosure booleans are not inferred from absence. GENIUS rulemaking is still underway: September 30 SCRC procedure is not whole-Act effectiveness, and the broad DASP restriction is scheduled for July 18, 2028.

sourcesChecked: Independent 2026-10-07 official-domain search for Bucket Protocol, Enosys, DJED and COTI with GENIUS across OCC, Federal Reserve, FDIC, NCUA and Treasury; no exact matching approval, qualification, application or registration announcement located.
negativeEvidenceReview.summary: As of 2026-10-07, no public GENIUS PPSI approval, state qualification, official pending application or registered foreign exception naming Bucket Protocol BUCK's exact issuer was located in the opened regulator materials and reviewed issuer sources. Public CDP mechanics do not establish a legal issuer obligated to redeem dollars or other fixed monetary value, so applicability remains unclear. This is a bounded negative-evidence finding, not an exhaustive private-application search or a determination of unlawful issuance.
